# ecoSynthesis (0.0.0.9000)

The goal of ecoSynthesis is to …

*This package is a work in progress and is not yet ready for use. Please
check back later for updates.*

Please find more information about the Environmental Indicators
Initiative here;
<https://ardc.edu.au/project/environmental-indicators-initiative/>, and
the Ecosystem Indicator Workflows project here;
<https://ardc.edu.au/project/ecosystem-indicator-workflows/>.

## Installation

You can install the development version of ecoSynthesis from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Ecosystem-Indicators-Workflows/ecoSynthesis")
```

## Example

This is a basic example which shows you how to solve a common problem:

``` r

library(ecoSynthesis)

input_table <- data.frame(
  re1 = c(
    "Semi-deciduous Forest",
    "Deciduous Forest",
    "Wet Montane Forest",
    "Dry Montane Forest"
  ),
  efg1 = c("T1.1", "T1.2", "T1.1", "T1.2"),
  memb1 = c(80, 80, 70, 50),
  efg2 = c("T1.2", "T1.1", "T1.3", "T1.3"),
  memb2 = c(20, 20, 30, 50)
)

membership_table(
  input_table,
  "re1",
  c("efg1", "efg2", "efg3"),
  c("memb1", "memb2"),
  target = "T1.3"
)
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`TASVEG_mini`](https://ecosystem-indicators-workflows.github.io/ecoSynthesis/reference/TASVEG_mini.md)
  : A subset of the TASVEG dataset for development and testing
- [`TASVEG_mini_expert_paired`](https://ecosystem-indicators-workflows.github.io/ecoSynthesis/reference/TASVEG_mini_expert_paired.md)
  : A subset of expert cross-reference table in paired-columns format
  for development and testing
- [`membership_table()`](https://ecosystem-indicators-workflows.github.io/ecoSynthesis/reference/membership_table.md)
  : Reshape membership table from wide to long format
- [`standardise_xref_pairs()`](https://ecosystem-indicators-workflows.github.io/ecoSynthesis/reference/standardise_xref_pairs.md)
  : Standardise column names for expert cross-reference data in
  paired-columns format.
